trust_decision.summary: The project decides that the default `eval: 'safe'` makes JSONPath filter/dynamic expressions non-executable; in Node that decision is implemented by aliasing `JSONPath.prototype.safeVm` to the whole `vm` module, which is not a security boundary, so any attacker-influenced path expression reaches `vm.Script.runInNewContext` and runs code.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary only says RCE; README.md:179-185 tells the reader that `safe` is a no-op in Node and is equivalent to native `vm.Script`, so the Node adapter's one-line `JSONPath.prototype.safeVm = vm` is the first place an engineer would look.

fix_sites.entry_point: `jsonpath-plus` Node import/require (package.json exports '.' import/require) and bin/jsonpath-cli.js
`SafeScript` named export of the Node entry (dist/index-node-esm.js:697, dist/index-node-cjs.cjs:700)
browser bundle `jsonpath-plus` (exports '.' browser/default conditions) and global.jsonpathBrowser used by the test suite
`SafeScript` named export and `JSONPath.prototype.safeVm` installed by the browser entry
`JSONPath()` / `jsonpath()` callable and `JSONPath.prototype.evaluate()` with default or `safe` eval
new shared `src/Safe-Script.js` that `safeVm` uses in every runtime
SafeEval member/call/identifier/assignment handlers reached from `_eval` via `runInNewContext`

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The AST evaluator is the browser-only implementation (the browser `vm`/CSP substitute); the advisory's PoC runs in Node through `vm`, so the browser `safe` evaluator and the low-level `SafeScript` class it backs can be argued to be out of scope and left untouched.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate safe-eval filters read and call inherited prototype functions: `$..[?(["book", "books"].includes(@property))]` (test/test.safe-eval.js:179) and sandbox functions such as `filter(@)` (test/test.safe-eval.js:119). An over-broad fix that blocks all inherited/prototype property reads or all function invocation (rather than only `constructor`/`__proto__` names) breaks documented, tested behaviour.

O6_input_shapes: computed non-string property value that coerces to a blocked name (`obj[['constructor']]`, value with custom `toString`)
bare identifier resolved through the sandbox object's prototype chain (`constructor`, `__proto__`)
assignment to `__proto__` through the assignment expression handler
member read on `null`/`undefined`, which must throw TypeError instead of escaping

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An extra `eval` mode (for example 'fast'/'safe2') that constructs a Script through `this.vm` for compatibility.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The dispatch is already an if/else chain over string, boolean and class forms; a new mode is a one-line maintainer change.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second platform entry (worker, Deno, edge/React-Native) that assigns `safeVm` to a Function-based shim instead of the AST evaluator.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: package.json:62-64 already special-cases react-native `vm: false`, so per-platform vm adapters are an established pattern here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A CSP fallback that compiles with `new Function` and is selected for `safe` when jsep cannot parse an expression.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Two Script classes already sit side by side in this file; a fallback for unsupported syntax is a natural extension.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A precompiled/persisted script path that reloads a `Script` instance or its source from `JSONPath.cache` without re-validating the expression.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: `JSONPath.cache` is a public global keyed by user code, so persisting compiled scripts is easy to add.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A handler for a new jsep node type (tagged template, optional chaining, sequence) that resolves a property by raw name without the constructor/__proto__ guard.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: SafeEval's switch grows expression type by expression type as jsep plugins are added, and each new node type lands here.

O9_family: code injection (CWE-94): attacker-controlled JSONPath filter/dynamic expression is evaluated as JavaScript, leading to remote code execution

O10_build.toolchain: npm or pnpm; rollup + babel + terser for the dist bundles; mocha + chai + c8 for tests; eslint; tsc/typedoc
O10_build.project_tests: test/test.safe-eval.js and test/test.eval.js each run twice ('Node vm' and 'JSONPath vm') through test-helpers/checkVM.js:17-41; test/test.cli.js drives bin/jsonpath-cli.js against dist; `npm test` = eslint + rollup + c8 + tsc

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Point Node's `safe` mode at the browser AST `SafeScript` (or just delete `JSONPath.prototype.safeVm = vm`); that evaluator still hands out `[].constructor.constructor` and still resolves `constructor` through the sandbox prototype chain.

out_of_scope_notes: `eval: 'native'` (src/jsonpath.js:662-663, browser `new Function` at src/jsonpath-browser.js:262) is documented as the deliberately unsafe opt-in (README.md:183-184), so it is not counted as an uncovered route.
